scenes.title: A fridge alarm must explain the gaps
lines: Cold-Chain Guard for QNX 8.0
Simulated sensor • QNX 8.0.0 x86_64 in QEMU
Recorded target console; not a new QEMU boot
scenes.say: A fridge alarm must explain what happened, and what it could not observe. We built Cold Chain Guard on QNX eight. These are actual saved QNX console results for the device and crash recovery checks. Our sensor is simulated. This is a software prototype, not a medical device.

scenes.title: One device, ordinary file operations
lines: Read /dev/fridge0: temperature, validity, alarm and advice
Write all limits atomically; reject invalid input
QNX resource manager + monotonic timer pulses
mono: coldchain: write and EINVAL atomicity verified
scenes.say: The resource manager exposes slash dev slash fridge zero. Reading returns a snapshot of temperature, validity, alarm state and advisory trend. Writing changes all limits atomically. Invalid input changes nothing. A monotonic timer delivers pulses to the dispatch loop, where sampling and device requests are serialized.

scenes.title: Scheduling and recovery, checked on QNX
lines: Fixed FIFO priority for dispatch and timer pulses
SLM restarts an abnormally terminated process
Pass/fail application checks; no QNX performance results
mono: coldchain: new serving process and restart acceptance PASS
scenes.say: The sampler and pulses use explicit fixed priority. Our application deadline checks pass under lower priority CPU load. SLM restarts an abnormally terminated daemon, and the test reads the device from a different serving process. The audit declares an unknown gap. These are fixture acceptance checks, not QNX performance results.

scenes.title: Advice cannot silence an alarm
lines: Explainable linear trend toward the configured limits
Sensor gaps and accepted limit writes reset the window
Alarm logic remains authoritative
scenes.say: The forecast fits a linear trend and offers advice about approaching a limit. A sensor gap or accepted limit change resets its window. Advice cannot delay, suppress or clear the alarm. The saved QNX forecast gate passed. Physical sensing and clinical suitability have not been validated.

scenes.title: Run the portable checks again
lines: Executed on the host during this render
C11 • strict warnings • AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
Selected literal output; full command exit checked separately
scenes.say: Now we run the portable checks on the host, using strict compiler warnings and sanitizers. These selected lines are real command output. The suite covers the state machine, device protocol, storage, forecast and host tools. Host execution supports the saved target evidence; it does not replace execution on QNX.

scenes.title: Replay the same input on the host
lines: Fresh host reference from the target scenario
CSV timestamps are synthetic input, not measured performance
M5 replay steps rows; it is separate from the live timer path
scenes.say: We validate the same scenario used on the target and generate a fresh host reference. This deterministic replay steps the production modules once per CSV row. Scenario timestamps are synthetic input, not measured platform performance. The live timer and resource manager have their own target tests.

scenes.title: Verify the real QNX serial export
lines: Saved QNX export: checksum, audit chain, host reference
The comparison also rejects a self-consistent truncated replay
scenes.say: Next we extract the real QNX serial export. The checksum verifies transfer, the audit verifier checks the chain, and the fresh host replay must match every byte. This closes the truncated replay case. A live audit still needs an external trusted anchor to detect a rewritten chain or valid tail removal.

scenes.title: Reproduce it. Then take it to hardware.
lines: Source: github.com/DesignMaster-Solutions/coldchain-guard-qnx
Codelab: github.com/DesignMaster-Solutions/qnx8-resmgr-codelab
Next: physical probe, persistent media, external notifications
Prototype only • no vaccine-safety or clinical claim
scenes.say: The verified target replay contains twenty one records. Our public source and companion codelab show how to build and boot with your own licensed SDP. Hardware sensing, power loss validation, external notifications and a staff acknowledgement interface remain future work. Follow the repository to reproduce the QEMU workflow. Built by Design Master Solutions, LLC.
